questions.explain: The more electronegative the halogen, the stronger its −I effect and the better it stabilises the carboxylate, so fluoroacetic acid is the strongest.

questions.q: Which acid has the lowest pKa?
questions.explain: The −I effect of Cl fades quickly with distance: pKa 2.86 (α), 4.05 (β), 4.52 (γ). The chlorine nearest the COOH group raises acidity most.

questions.q: Which group shows the strongest −I effect?
questions.explain: Positively charged groups head the −I list: –NH₃⁺ > –NO₂ > –CN > … > –F.

questions.q: Taking only the inductive effect into account, the correct order of stability of carbanions is
questions.explain: +I alkyl groups intensify a negative charge, so each extra alkyl group destabilises a carbanion; the order is the reverse of that for carbocations.
